subtitle: A young voice in the dark, carrying a nation’s last open call to freedom

panels.shot: low-angle medium close-up framed by darkened walls and a glowing radio transmitter
panels.action: Usha Mehta leans over a makeshift transmitter in a dim Bombay room, headphones on, eyes fierce and steady as valve tubes glow around her like embers in the night.

dialogue.text: August 1942: as Congress leaders vanish into prisons overnight, a young student named Usha Mehta dares to keep Gandhi’s ‘Do or Die’ alive on an illegal voice in the dark.

i18n.hi: अगस्त 1942: जब काँग्रेस नेता रातों-रात जेलों में गायब हुए, तब उषा मेहता नाम की छात्रा ने ग़ैरक़ानूनी रेडियो पर गांधी का ‘करो या मरो’ ज़िंदा रखा।

panels.shot: wide aerial over Bombay’s Gowalia Tank Maidan at dusk
panels.action: A vast crowd fills Gowalia Tank Maidan under a humid August sky, torchlight and tricolour flags rising around a small, distant platform.

dialogue.text: On 8 August 1942, in Bombay’s Gowalia Tank Maidan, Gandhi’s words cut through monsoon air: a call to ‘Do or Die’ that would throw India into its deepest confrontation with the Raj.

i18n.hi: 8 अगस्त 1942, बॉम्बे के गोवालिया टैंक मैदान में, मानसून चीरते गांधी के अल्फ़ाज़: ‘करो या मरो’ की ऐसी पुकार, जिसने राज को सीधी टक्कर दी।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a British police raid at night
panels.action: Under harsh lantern light, British police and soldiers rush into a darkened building, arresting shadowy Indian leaders as files and papers lie scattered.

dialogue.text: By dawn, the call’s echo was cut short. Gandhi, Nehru, Patel, almost the entire Congress high command, seized and sealed away. The Raj hoped the movement would die before it began.

i18n.hi: सुबह तक गूँज दबा दी गई। गांधी, नेहरू, पटेल, लगभग पूरा काँग्रेस नेतृत्व, पकड़कर बंद कर दिया गया। राज को यक़ीन था कि आंदोलन जन्म से पहले ही मर जाएगा।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Usha in a crowded student hostel corridor
panels.action: In a narrow hostel corridor, young Usha Mehta listens tensely as other students whisper of arrests and crackdowns, her hands clenched around a folded newspaper.

dialogue.text: In this silence, twenty-something Usha Mehta, a law student from a Gandhian home, heard only one thing: a voice ordering her to act when all voices seemed cut off.

i18n.hi: इस सन्नाटे में, बीस-पचीस की उषा मेहता ने बस एक ही बात सुनी: जब सब आवाजें काट दी जाएँ, तब उठ खड़ी होने का हुक्म।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot of Usha and comrades poring over a crude radio diagram
panels.action: Around a bare table in a cramped Bombay room, Usha and a few young men hunch over a rough circuit sketch and scattered radio parts, faces lit by a single lamp.

dialogue.text: The police had silenced Congress papers and meetings. So Usha and a handful of friends turned to a newer weapon, a fragile thing of coils and valves: the clandestine radio.

i18n.hi: पुलिस ने काँग्रेस के अख़बार और मीटिंगें चुप करा दीं। तो उषा और चंद साथी पहुँचे एक नए हथियार तक—कॉइलों और वाल्वों की नाज़ुक चीज़: गुप्त रेडियो।

panels.shot: tight shot on hands tuning a home-made transmitter
panels.action: Close on Usha’s steady hands as she adjusts dials and wires on a home-built transmitter, a hand-painted note beside it reading only a frequency in pencil.

dialogue.text: They found a narrow window on the airwaves, around 42.34 metres. From there, if they could stay hidden, they would speak as ‘Congress Radio’ to a nation cut off from its leaders.

i18n.hi: उन्हें हवा में एक पतली सी खिड़की मिली, करीब 42.34 मीटर पर। वहीं से, अगर छिपे रह सके, तो ‘काँग्रेस रेडियो’ बनकर नेताओं से कटी क़ौम से बात कर सकते थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Usha seated at the microphone on 14 August
panels.action: On 14 August 1942, Usha sits upright before a simple microphone, headphones on, lips parted, as a comrade signals silently that the transmitter is live.

dialogue.text: On 14 August, four days after Gandhi’s arrest, a clear, young voice broke into crackling sets: ‘This is the Congress Radio, calling on 42.34 metres… from somewhere in India.’

i18n.hi: 14 अगस्त को, गांधी की गिरफ़्तारी के चार दिन बाद, चरमराते सेटों पर एक साफ, कमसिन आवाज़ गूँजी: ‘यह है काँग्रेस रेडियो, 42.34 मीटर पर… हिंदुस्तान के किसी कोने से।’

panels.shot: montage wide of villagers and townsfolk listening to a radio
panels.action: In a thatched village hut, a small town shop, and a railway waiting room, people cluster around radios, faces intent as the same unseen voice flows through them.

dialogue.text: Across towns and villages, people leaned over borrowed sets. Instead of official bulletins, they now heard banned speeches, underground reports, and word that the struggle still breathed.

i18n.hi: कस्बों–गाँवों में लोग उधार के रेडियो पर झुक गए। सरकारी बुलेटिन की जगह अब उन्हें बंद किए गए भाषण, ज़मीनी रिपोर्टें और यह खबर सुनाई दी कि जंग अभी ज़िंदा है।

panels.shot: wide shot of British officials in a colonial office examining radio direction-finding equipment
panels.action: In a high-ceilinged colonial office, British officers bend over a map of Bombay dotted with pins, as a radio direction-finding set hums beside them.

dialogue.text: In Delhi and Bombay, the Viceroy’s men bristled. Reports warned London that this was the gravest rising since 1857. Now a rebel radio was threading the scattered sparks together.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली–बॉम्बे में वायसराय के लोग तिलमिला उठे। रिपोर्टें लंदन को चेताने लगीं कि यह 1857 के बाद की सबसे बड़ी बग़ावत है। अब एक बाग़ी रेडियो बिखरी चिंगारियों को जोड़ रहा था।

panels.shot: dynamic tracking shot following police and technicians through Bombay streets
panels.action: British police and technicians sweep through crowded Bombay streets with portable antennas, the city’s tram wires and balconies looming over their hurried search.

dialogue.text: Teams with listening sets hunted the signal through Bombay’s maze. Each time they closed in, the station seemed to vanish, only to reappear from another unknown room.

i18n.hi: सुनने वाले सेट लिए टीमें बॉम्बे की भूलभुलैया में सिग्नल सूँघने निकलीं। हर बार जैसे ही पास पहुँचीं, स्टेशन ग़ायब; फिर किसी और अनजान कमरे से उभर आता।

panels.shot: wide interior shot of a room being hurriedly dismantled
panels.action: Usha and her comrades hastily coil wires, lift a small transmitter, and slip out of a modest flat as a landlord watches anxiously from the doorway.

dialogue.text: Usha later recalled those weeks as a moving shadow. Flats changed, helpers rotated, equipment wrapped and carried in plain crates. To stay alive, the Congress Radio could never sleep in one place.

i18n.hi: उषा ने बाद में उन हफ़्तों को चलती परछाईं कहा। मकान बदलते, मददगार घूमते, सामान सादे बक्सों में लिपटा उठता–उतरता। ज़िंदा रहने के लिए काँग्रेस रेडियो एक जगह सो ही नहीं सकता था।

panels.shot: split wide panel contrasting different regions: Bihar railway, Midnapore countryside, Satara village
panels.action: A split scene shows a sabotaged railway track in Bihar, a smoky village in Midnapore under circling aircraft, and a quiet Satara village square with villagers conferring under a tree.

dialogue.text: Beyond Bombay, the call spread in uneven waves. In Bihar and Midnapore, protests met harsh reprisals, even aerial bombing. In Satara, villagers began experimenting with their own ‘parallel government’.

i18n.hi: बॉम्बे से बाहर, पुकार टेढ़ी–मेढ़ी लहरों में फैली। बिहार और मिदनापुर में आंदोलनों पर सख़्त दमन, यहाँ तक कि हवाई बमबारी। सतारा में गाँववालों ने अपना ‘समानांतर सरकार’ आज़माना शुरू किया।

panels.shot: medium shot of local leaders in Satara discussing under a tree
panels.action: Under a spreading tree in Satara district, local leaders sit in a circle, discussing by lantern-light as villagers look on, while a British police outpost stands faintly in the distance.

dialogue.text: In the hills around Satara, Nana Patil and others organised what later came to be called a ‘Prati Sarkar’—a practical answer to Gandhi’s call to make the Raj’s authority irrelevant on the ground.

i18n.hi: सतारा की पहाड़ियों में नाना पाटिल वगैरह ने वह रचा, जिसे बाद में ‘प्रति सरकार’ कहा गया—ज़मीन पर राज की हुकूमत को बेकार करने वाला गांधी की पुकार का ठोस जवाब।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Jayaprakash Narayan slipping past a prison wall at night
panels.action: In the darkness by a prison wall, the slim figure of Jayaprakash Narayan lowers himself with a rope, a distant searchlight sweeping just past him.

dialogue.text: Elsewhere, activists like Jayaprakash Narayan slipped out of jails and went underground. The movement looked leaderless from above, but local networks were improvising their own centres of gravity.

i18n.hi: दूसरी तरफ़, जयप्रकाश नारायण जैसे कार्यकर्ता जेलों से फिसलकर ज़मीन के नीचे चले गए। ऊपर से आंदोलन बिन–नेता दिखता, पर नीचे–नीचे अपने स्थानीय गुरुत्व–केंद्र गढ़ रहा था।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Usha reading from a paper into the mic
panels.action: Back in a secret Bombay room, Usha reads calmly from a handwritten sheet into the microphone, while a comrade times the broadcast with a pocket watch.

dialogue.text: Night after night, the Congress Radio stitched these scattered acts into a single story, carrying news from Satara, Bihar, Midnapore, and messages from leaders now locked away.

i18n.hi: रात दर रात, काँग्रेस रेडियो ने ये बिखरे कारनामे जोड़कर एक कहानी बनाई—सतारा, बिहार, मिदनापुर से खबरें, और अब बंद हो चुके नेताओं के संदेश लेकर।

panels.shot: medium shot of British soldiers detaining villagers in a rural area
panels.action: In a dusty Bihar village lane, British soldiers herd a line of villagers toward a makeshift camp, while houses stand shuttered and fields lie untended.

dialogue.text: British records speak of tens of thousands, perhaps over sixty thousand, arrested in those months. Collective punishments fell on villages accused of sheltering saboteurs or listening to seditious broadcasts.

i18n.hi: ब्रिटिश रिकॉर्डों में उन महीनों में दसियों हज़ार, शायद साठ हज़ार से ऊपर गिरफ़्तारों का ज़िक्र है। पूरे–के–पूरे गाँव, सबोटाजियों को छुपाने या ‘राज–द्रोही’ प्रसारण सुनने के इल्ज़ाम में सज़ाएँ झेलते रहे।

panels.shot: tense medium shot of Usha noticing something wrong with a courier
panels.action: Usha glances sharply at a man entering the safe house doorway, her eyes narrowing as she senses unease, while the man avoids her gaze.

dialogue.text: The net, though, crept tighter. Direction-finders narrowed the radius. Informers hovered. One day, a courier’s hesitation, a face she could not quite place, became the crack through which danger entered.

i18n.hi: पर जाल भी कसता गया। दिशा नापने वाले सेटों ने घेरा छोटा किया। मुख़बिर मंडराने लगे। एक दिन, एक दूत की हिचक, एक चेहरा जो पहचाना सा होकर भी अनजान लगा—यही दरार बनी, जहाँ से ख़तरा अंदर घुसा।

panels.shot: wide shot of police raiding the safe house
panels.action: British police burst into the clandestine room as comrades rise in alarm; Usha stands by the transmitter, shoulders squared, as hands reach for the equipment.

dialogue.speaker: usha_mehta
dialogue.text: If you seize this box, you cannot seize the words already heard.

i18n.hi: अगर आप ये डिब्बा छीन भी लें, जो सुन लिया गया, उसे नहीं छीन सकते।

panels.shot: medium shot in an interrogation room with Usha seated opposite officers
panels.action: In a stark interrogation room, Usha sits straight-backed on a wooden chair, facing British officers across a bare table, her face composed and unreadable.

dialogue.text: In custody, she faced questions about names, locations, funding. Later, she spoke of those sessions with the same quiet tone: she had chosen this path when she chose to broadcast.

i18n.hi: कस्टडी में उस पर नाम, ठिकानों, पैसों की बौछार सवालों की हुई। बाद में भी उसने वही धीमी आवाज़ रखी: जब रेडियो चालू किया, उसी दिन ये रास्ता भी चुन लिया था।

panels.shot: wide shot of a courtroom or formal hearing with Usha standing
panels.action: In a colonial courtroom, Usha stands in the dock, small against the high wooden railings and robed officials, as spectators strain to see her.

dialogue.text: The station had lived for eighty-seven days. Now, in the files of the Raj, it became a ‘conspiracy’, its young operators labelled offenders rather than broadcasters keeping a political resolution alive.

i18n.hi: स्टेशन अस्सी–सात दिन जिया। अब राज की फ़ाइलों में वह ‘साज़िश’ बना, और उसके जवान ऑपरेटर, एक प्रस्ताव को ज़िंदा रखने वाले उद्घोषक नहीं, अपराधी दर्ज हुए।

panels.shot: montage of documents and later-era scholars in archives
panels.action: A layered image shows wartime British reports, typed in stiff language, overlaid with the faint figures of modern historians reading files in a quiet archive.

dialogue.text: For decades, the Quit India rising was often described as chaotic and leaderless. Regional archives and oral histories slowly revealed another pattern: improvised self-rule and underground coordination.

i18n.hi: सालों तक भारत छोड़ो आंदोलन को बेसिर–पैर और बिन–नेता बताया गया। मगर सूबे के रिकॉर्ड और ज़बानी यादों ने धीरे–धीरे दूसरा नक्शा दिखाया: खुद–बनाई हुकूमतें और ज़मीन के नीचे का समन्वय।

panels.shot: gentle medium shot of an older Usha giving an oral history interview
panels.action: Years later, an older Usha sits in a simple sari before a tape recorder in a quiet room, speaking softly as a researcher listens and takes notes.

dialogue.text: In later years, Usha Mehta would remember not the thrill, but the responsibility—that each broadcast might reassure or endanger, and that the risk was accepted with open eyes.

i18n.hi: आगे के बरसों में, उषा मेहता को रोमांच नहीं, ज़िम्मेदारी याद रही—कि हर प्रसारण किसी को दिलासा भी दे सकता था, किसी को ख़तरे में भी डाल सकता था; और उन्होंने यह रिस्क आँखें खोलकर लिया था।

panels.shot: low-angle silhouette of young Usha at the mic dissolving into the map of India
panels.action: The silhouette of young Usha at a microphone dissolves into the outline of India, faint radio waves radiating outward into darkness.

dialogue.text: Her signal was eventually silenced, but in that brief window, it showed how, when doors were bolted shut, a single hidden voice could still bind a vast, fractured land to a common decision.

i18n.hi: आख़िर उसका सिग्नल चुप करा दिया गया, पर उस छोटे से वक़्फ़े में उसने दिखा दिया कि जब दरवाज़े बंद कर दिए जाएँ, तब भी एक छिपी हुई आवाज़ टूटी–फूटी, फैली धरती को एक फैसले में बाँध सकती है।

subtitle_i18n.en: A young voice in the dark, carrying a nation’s last open call to freedom
subtitle_i18n.hi: अँधेरे में एक नौजवान आवाज़, जो आज़ादी की आखिरी पुकार उठा रही है
